rotation.title: The rotation
rotation.intent: This is the priority list every section above compares you against. None of it is about your pull — read it when a number above looks wrong to you.
rotation.economy: Two things shape the list. Your global cooldown is a flat second — haste never shortens it, because none of these is a spell; haste buys energy instead. And chi comes slower than globals: Jab costs 40 energy for 2 chi, and energy refills at about ten a second, so a global earns you two thirds of a chi. Two presses in three have to be chi-free. The rest is about caps. Energy caps at 100 and the bank at 20, and nine entries do nothing but keep energy from overcapping. A full bar earns you nothing.

tigereyeBrew.title: Do you have the Rune of Re-Origination?
tigereyeBrew.detail: One button, two rule sets; which one applies depends on whether you have the trinket. A stack costs three chi and a brew spends ten, so the bank fills slowly — the branches disagree only about whether anything is worth waiting for.

talent.title: Which of the three you took
talent.detail: One talent row, so only one of these is ever on your bar. All three do the same job: a global that costs neither chi nor energy, taken only when the bar has room to spare. Their order never matters, because you can only have one.

blackoutKick.title: How much the dump has to leave behind
blackoutKick.detail: One entry with two energy reserves in it, and the number of enemies decides between them: how much has to stay in the bar depends on what else there is to spend it on.

risingSunKick.title: Whether the pack has pushed the kick down the list
risingSunKick.detail: One entry with two halves, and the target count decides which applies — but only from two enemies up. At one the entry is skipped outright and the kick drops to its unconditional rung further down. At two it is pressed on cooldown. From three, the buttons above it beat one kick, and only the debuff running out still triggers this rung.

touchOfDeath.name: Touch of Death
touchOfDeath.test: The target's health drops below yours
touchOfDeath.why: It deals a lump equal to your own maximum health, for one global. The list presses Fortifying Brew with it, because that raises the number it rolls against.

chiBrew.name: Chi Brew
chiBrew.test: 2 chi below cap, in the opener or under a brew
chiBrew.why: Two chi for no global. Those two chi save you a Jab, and a Jab you skip is 40 energy left in a bar that was already close to full.

tigereyeBrewRune.name: Tigereye Brew
tigereyeBrewRune.test: A proc is a global from ending and the bank beats it
tigereyeBrewRune.why: With the Rune on, the brew is a snapshot tool and little else. It reads your mastery once and holds it fifteen seconds, so spending it on the proc's last global is what makes the proc's stats outlive the proc — see below. Every other condition stops the bank overflowing while it waits.

tigereyeBrewBank.name: Tigereye Brew
tigereyeBrewBank.test: No brew running and the bank is at 19
tigereyeBrewBank.why: With nothing to snapshot, the only failure left is overflow: 20 is the ceiling, and every stack earned past it is three chi spent for nothing. The two chi is a floor on the state you spend it in — fifteen seconds of buff are worth less off an empty bar.

energizingBrew.name: Energizing Brew
energizingBrew.why: Sixty energy poured into a nearly full bar is sixty energy gone. Bloodlust already refills the bar faster than a flat one-second global can empty it, so the two overlap into waste.

invokeXuen.name: Invoke Xuen
invokeXuen.why: Nothing. It is the only entry with no condition at all, so the only cost of holding it is a summon that never fits into the fight.

risingSunKickCooldown.name: Rising Sun Kick
risingSunKickCooldown.test: There is a second enemy, and the cooldown is up
risingSunKickCooldown.why: The debuff, not the kick — see below. It is the only button here that makes everything else you press hit harder, and a second enemy is what makes it worth a rung this high.

risingSunKickHold.name: Rising Sun Kick
risingSunKickHold.test: Its debuff is a global from expiring
risingSunKickHold.why: Holding the debuff, not landing the kick. From three targets the buttons above hit the whole pack and beat one kick, so the list lets it slide — but never far enough to drop the 20% it is lifting everything by.

tigerPalmRefresh.name: Tiger Palm
tigerPalmRefresh.test: Tiger Power has a second or less left
tigerPalmRefresh.why: Tiger Power ignores 30% of the target's armour for 20 seconds. It does not stack, so pressing with a healthy buff up throws the rest of it away and takes a global Jab wanted.

chiWave.name: Chi Wave
chiWave.test: Cooldown up, energy a second from full
chiWave.why: It costs nothing, which is the problem: a global that generates no energy, spent while the bar is about to cap, is a Jab you could not afford to skip.

zenSphere.name: Zen Sphere
zenSphere.test: Cooldown up, energy spare, under two spheres
zenSphere.why: Two spheres is the cap, so a third press replaces one still ticking. Its energy check is twice Chi Wave's — two seconds of headroom, not one — which is why it sits at a lower rung.

chiBurst.name: Chi Burst
chiBurst.test: Cooldown up, energy a global from full
chiBurst.why: The same check as Chi Wave and the same reason for it, on twice the cooldown: half as many presses over a pull, so half as much to lose by holding one.

comboBreakerKick.name: Blackout Kick
comboBreakerKick.test: Combo Breaker has made it free
comboBreakerKick.why: A chi-free spender, which is the thing this list is permanently short of. The proc lasts 15 seconds, so there is no hurry — and no reason to let it lapse either.

fistsOfFury.name: Fists of Fury
fistsOfFury.test: Energy will not cap, and no brew or proc says hold
fistsOfFury.why: The most damage chi can buy, and four seconds doing nothing else — your auto-attacks are held for the whole channel too. All three conditions exist to stop those four seconds swallowing something.

tigerPalmProc.name: Tiger Palm
tigerPalmProc.test: A free palm, past the opener, with room to spend it
tigerPalmProc.why: The same free-global logic as the kick, several rungs lower. Tiger Palm hits weakly, so a free one only earns its global when there is nothing better to put in it.

jab.name: Jab
jab.test: Two or more chi below the cap
jab.why: Two below, not one. Jab returns two chi, so pressing it one short of the cap throws the second away. Everything above it spends what this generated.

rushingJadeWind.name: Rushing Jade Wind
rushingJadeWind.test: Energy is a second from capping, or the pull is under 75s
rushingJadeWind.why: 40 energy on a six-second cooldown, and down here it is no longer free filler. Past 75 seconds this rung fires only to stop the bar overflowing, so the 40 it costs is energy that was about to be thrown away. At two targets the rung near the top takes over instead.

blackoutKick.name: Blackout Kick
blackoutKick.test: 35 energy still banked when the kick returns
blackoutKick.why: The chi dump, and the only entry that looks ahead. Spending chi here is right only if what is left still covers the Jabs the next Rising Sun Kick needs.

stormEarthAndFire.name: Storm, Earth and Fire
stormEarthAndFire.test: One clone at 2 targets, two at 3+
stormEarthAndFire.why: A clone cuts everyone's damage, yours included: to 60% each with one out, 45% each with two. One clone across two enemies is 120% of your damage, two across three is 135%. At one enemy there is nowhere to put a clone, so it is pure loss and the list never casts it.

rushingJadeWindMulti.name: Rushing Jade Wind
rushingJadeWindMulti.test: The dot is not already spinning
rushingJadeWindMulti.why: It moves above Rising Sun Kick. The wind hits everything for as long as it spins and the kick hits one, so the second enemy is roughly where they cross. From three it returns a chi as well.

spinningCraneKick.name: Spinning Crane Kick
spinningCraneKick.why: It moves above Fists of Fury. Fists splits one lump evenly across everything in front of you, so its total never grows with the pack; this one's does. Three is where the growing one passes the fixed one.

blackoutKickDump.name: Blackout Kick
blackoutKickDump.test: 105 energy still banked when the kick returns
blackoutKickDump.why: With Spinning Crane Kick in the list there is far more worth spending energy on, so the chi dump has to leave three times as much behind before it fires.

craneOverKick.name: Spinning Crane Kick
craneOverKick.test: The kick's debuff is safe for another 2.25 seconds
craneOverKick.why: Now it goes above Rising Sun Kick as well. The 2.25 seconds is what keeps the debuff from being lost to it: at four targets the kick is delayed, not dropped.

risingSunKickMulti.name: Rising Sun Kick
risingSunKickMulti.why: It never leaves the list, because the debuff lifts everything else you press. Nothing drops the kick — the refresh above it, and from three the pack buttons, only delay it.

notes.snapshot: Tigereye Brew reads your mastery once, when the buff goes up, and never again. That is why the priority list spends it on the last global of a Re-Origination proc: the proc's ten seconds of converted stats are frozen into a fifteen-second buff and carried on after the proc has gone.
notes.channel: Nothing else in the list is read while Fists of Fury channels — not a brew, not a cooldown, not the debuff. Four seconds is long enough for a cooldown to come up, a proc to land and the debuff to fall off with nothing done about any of them.
notes.debuff: Rising Sun Kick's debuff goes on every enemy, not just the one you kicked, and lifts all your abilities by 20% for fifteen seconds — auto-attacks aside. Losing it costs a sixth of that, across the whole pack, for as long as it is down.
notes.talents: The list assumes two talent choices and skips the entries you did not take. Rushing Jade Wind and Invoke Xuen share a row, so you can never have both — which is why they are two rungs above rather than a fork. Chi Wave, Zen Sphere and Chi Burst share a row too, drawn as a fork wherever this log cannot tell which you brought.
notes.inferred: A rung only leaves the flow above on proof that the button was not on your bar. A log carries no talent tree, so a button you never pressed is exactly the one you may have forgotten — an unpressed rung is never removed. What is removed is the alternative to something you did press: a Spinning Crane Kick rules out Rushing Jade Wind, and a Chi Wave settles the row it shares with Zen Sphere and Chi Burst.
notes.mastery: One correction, because the name misleads. Your mastery in this patch is Bottled Fury, and all it does is make each Tigereye Brew stack hit harder. There is no alternating-ability mastery here — Combo Strikes belongs to a later expansion — so pressing the same button twice in a row costs you nothing.
notes.jadeWind: Rushing Jade Wind is on the list twice, and the two are not alternatives. Entry 17 lifts it above Rising Sun Kick as soon as there is a second enemy and tests nothing else. Entry 31 keeps it near the bottom and fires when energy is a second from capping, the pull is under 75 seconds, or Bloodlust and Energizing Brew are both active. It costs 40, the same as a Jab, and returns one chi where Jab returns two. So the higher rung spends generator energy on AoE, and the lower rung uses overflow or the haste window. Its own six-second cooldown, re-armed to whatever is left of the dot, keeps that from being every global.
notes.cooldowns: Elemental Mastery and Ascendance are off the global, so the ladder never walks them — each still has its own section.
notes.raid: Skull Banner, Stormlash Totem, Bloodlust and the racials are left off the list: they are raid calls or once-a-fight buttons, not a decision about your next global.

takeaways.title: Key improvements
takeaways.clean: Nothing came out below its target, so there is no short list to give you. The detail on each is further down the page.

snapshotRate.fix: You brewed on the last global of {{value, percent}} of your Re-Origination windows. Aim for {{target, percent}} — brewing one global early loses the proc's strongest seconds.

rskUptime.fix: The debuff was up for {{value, percent}} of the time you could reach a target, against {{target, percent}}. It raises everything else you do, so a gap costs more than the kick itself.

brewStacks.fix: Your brews averaged {{value, decimal}} stacks. A brew can spend a maximum of 10, and {{target, decimal}} is the target — every stack below that is lost damage.

brewShortUses.label: Wait for the tenth stack
brewShortUses.fix: You spent {{value, integer}} of your Tigereye Brews with the bank under ten, with no Re-Origination proc about to run out and more than fifteen seconds of fight still to come. Those two are the only reasons to brew short. Hold the rest until the bank reads ten.

brewCapWaste.fix: {{value, integer}} stacks were earned with the bank already full, so they never landed. Spend a brew before the bank caps and the next stacks have somewhere to go.

potionsUsed.fix: {{value, integer}}/{{target, integer}} potions used. One goes down in the last second before the pull, the next a minute in when it comes off cooldown.

energizingBrewRjw.label: Use Energizing Brew with RJW
energizingBrewRjw.fix: Bloodlust or Time Warp was up with Rushing Jade Wind talented, but you did not press Energizing Brew. From two targets up the rotation allows both together, and the extra energy is worth most in AoE.

flameShockUptime.label: Keep the dot up
flameShockUptime.fix: Flame Shock was up for {{value, percent}} of the time you had something to hit, against {{target, percent}}. Lava Burst needs that dot on the target, so a gap costs more than the dot itself.

flameShockWaste.label: Stop overwriting the dot
flameShockWaste.fix: {{value, percent}} of your Flame Shock refreshes bought nothing — they were not in the dot’s last tick, not Ascendance prep, and did not snapshot a stronger dot. Keep it under {{target, percent}}; those globals could have been Lightning Bolts.

flameShockMultiDot.label: Dot the second target
flameShockMultiDot.fix: The dot was up on the secondary target for {{value, percent}} of the time two enemies were up, against {{target, percent}}. The gap is damage the second dot would have done.

earthShockGood.label: Spend the shocks right
earthShockGood.fix: {{value, percent}} of your Earth Shocks went out with the shield charged up and the dot still long, against {{target, percent}}. An early shock spends the shield the next proc wants.

searingTotemUptime.label: Keep the totem ticking
searingTotemUptime.fix: Searing Totem was up for {{value, percent}} of the time it could have been, against {{target, percent}}. It is one global for a minute of damage.

searingTotemOverlaps.label: Keep the summons apart
searingTotemOverlaps.fix: Searing Totem was placed under the Fire Elemental on {{value, integer}} of your presses. The Fire Elemental replaces the totem the instant it lands, so a press under it buys nothing.

fireElementalPrepull.label: Summon before the pull
fireElementalPrepull.fix: The Fire Elemental was not out when the pull started. Summoning it in the last second before the pull gets you its whole minute from the first second, and starts its five-minute cooldown that much earlier. This log cannot see whether it was still down from the attempt before, so a late summon is not counted against the pull.

flameShockSnapshots.label: Catch the proc windows
flameShockSnapshots.fix: You refreshed Flame Shock inside {{value, percent}} of your proc windows, against {{target, percent}}. A missed window is a snapshot that never got its spellpower.

lightningShieldOvercap.label: Spend the shield
lightningShieldOvercap.fix: The shield sat at seven for {{value, duration}} past the grace. A shield at seven is a shock not taken, and every Lightning Bolt after that is Rolling Thunder with nowhere to put its charge.

lightningShieldFellOff.label: Keep the shield up
lightningShieldFellOff.fix: The shield came all the way off you — {{value, integer}} in a pull where it should be none. A full removal throws the whole counter away and the shield has to be rebuilt from one.

thunderstormMissed.label: Press Thunderstorm when you are dry
thunderstormMissed.fix: You spent {{value, duration}} at or under 15% mana with Thunderstorm off cooldown. It is free, hands back 15% of your maximum, and at that mana your next Lava Burst may not go out at all. Press it at 15%.

shamanisticRageMissed.label: Put Shamanistic Rage down
shamanisticRageMissed.fix: Shamanistic Rage came back to a pool already at or under 70% and went unpressed, on {{value, integer}} of its returns. It costs no global and cuts what your casts cost for fifteen seconds. Press it whenever it is up and you are under 70%.

fireElementalHasteUptime.label: Cover the haste cooldown
fireElementalHasteUptime.fix: The Fire Elemental was out for {{value, percent}} of your raid's haste cooldown, against {{target, percent}}. Its minute outlasts the lust's forty seconds, so a summon already standing when the lust lands covers all of it — press it last before the pull, not first after it. Do not glyph it: thirty seconds cannot cover forty, and the second elemental the glyph buys is worth less than the procs the first one gives up.

jadeWind.title: Rushing Jade Wind
jadeWind.intent: At one target, Invoke Xuen is the better level-90 choice and Rushing Jade Wind is a damage loss: its 40 energy buys one chi where a Jab buys two. It is worth a single-target press when that energy would otherwise hit the cap, on a pull shorter than 75 seconds, or while Bloodlust and Energizing Brew are both active. From two enemies up, it is your AoE and should be kept spinning — taking it removes Spinning Crane Kick from your bars.

lightningShield.aoeNote: The greyed stretches are the ones with three or more enemies up. The AoE priority list has no Earth Shock in it at all, so those seconds are left out of the overcap figure rather than counted against you. At two enemies the figure still holds you to it, because that list does spend the shield, just at six stacks instead of seven. Dropping the shield counts throughout either way: Rolling Thunder returns 2% of your maximum mana per charge and only while the buff is up, so keeping it up is right at every target count.

stormlash.title: Stormlash Totem
stormlash.intent: Stormlash does not stack. With more than one shaman in the raid you stagger the totems — first, then second, then third — so a totem dropped on top of one that is still running is a totem wasted.

stormlash.sourceNote: The two tiles and the chart above read where the raid laid its totems, which comes from a separate fetch this pull does not carry — so they count zero. The table below asks the other half of the question and needs no extra fetch: every totem whose buff landed on you, and who laid it.
stormlash.ascendanceNote: Dropping Stormlash costs you a global, and during Ascendance you want that global on Lava Beam — so lay the totem before you press Ascendance, or after the window closes. Treat this as a preference rather than a requirement: nothing in your score moves either way, and a totem still running through Ascendance is a good thing, because Stormlash pays out on what the raid does while it is up.
stormlash.note: The overlap row shows where two totems ran at once. The assignment is yours to make; the second totem in one of those stretches bought the raid nothing.

lavaBurst.title: Lava Burst
lavaBurst.intent: Lava Surge makes one Lava Burst free, and Ascendance takes its cooldown away entirely — those are the only two ways the button comes back early. Press Lava Burst while the surge is still up: a surge that expires with no Lava Burst inside it is a free cast thrown away, and a cast count will never show it to you.

lavaBurst.caption: What this pull gave away: Lava Surge procs that expired with no Lava Burst inside them, and Lava Bursts you pressed with no Flame Shock on the enemy you aimed at
lavaBurst.none: Nothing given away — every Lava Surge was spent, and every Lava Burst went out with Flame Shock already on its target.
lavaBurst.note: Flame Shock is what makes Lava Burst hit hard: a ×1.5 on the damage, and the crit is unconditional, so the two are one bonus and not two. The bonus is settled when the cast goes out, not when the missile lands — a dot that runs out during the ~0.8s of travel has already paid for the hit, so a press this section leaves alone can still look wrong if you expect the dot to survive to impact. So it is the completion that decides the row: every press that finished with no dot on its target is listed here, including one you committed onto a dot with less than a cast time left — that dot was gone by the instant the bonus was read. The priority list refuses that press as well, at the moment you made it, and the two charges are not the same charge: one is the choice and this one is the outcome.
